Based on my research, the unique Irish athletics family where **father, son, and daughter** were all capped for Ireland is the **Hopkins family**. Here are the details:

## **The Hopkins Family**

| Family Member | Role | First Cap Year | Event/Competition |
|--------------|------|---------------|-------------------|
| **Tom Hopkins** | Father | **1938** | International Cross Country, Belfast (2 April 1938) |
| **Tommy Hopkins** | Son | **1967** | International Cross Country, Barry (18 March 1967) |
| **Emily Hopkins** (née Hopkins, married name Dowling) | Daughter | **1967** | International Cross Country, Barry (18 March 1967) |

### Key Facts:
- **Tom Hopkins** (born 19 July 1910) made his international debut in 1938 when he was 28 years old
- **Tommy Hopkins** (born 14 July 1947) followed 29 years later, making his debut at age 19 in 1967
- **Emily Hopkins** (later Dowling) also made her debut in **1967**, just weeks after her brother Tommy, at age approximately 15-16
- All three competed in cross country events, primarily through Sportsworld AC in Dublin

This family holds the distinction of being the only Irish athletics family with three generations (father, son, and daughter) all representing Ireland at senior international level. They are officially recorded in Athletics Ireland's statistics as one of the few families with "Multiple Ireland caps from one family."

*Note: There is a separate famous British athlete named Thelma Hopkins (Olympic silver medalist 1956) but she competed for Northern Ireland/Great Britain, not the Irish athletics team.*

# Dooney Family Join Prestigious List - Athletics Ireland
## Dooney Family Join Prestigious List
#### Dooney Family Become the 13th Father and Son to be Capped for Ireland at Senior Level
*Information compiled by Pierce O’Callaghan
Following on from Tuesday’s announcement that Conor Dooney (Raheny Shamrock AC) will now represent Ireland at the European Cross Country Championships in Bulgaria, the Dooney family have made a bit of history of their own. Conor’s father Roy Dooney was capped 19 times for Ireland at senior level. Together they become the 13th father and son to be capped for Ireland at senior level since 1876. Making it a real family affair younger brother Kevin will also be in the team representing Ireland in the U23 race in Bulgaria.

# Dooney Family Join Prestigious List - Athletics Ireland
## Dooney Family Join Prestigious List
#### Previous Father and Son Caps
The previous time this happened was earlier in the year with Eamon and John Coghlan when John gained his first cap at the Penn Relays in April. They join current father & son combinations of Tim & Timmy Crowe, Brendan & Shane Quinn, Paul & Colin Quirke.
Sara Treacy is the daughter of Siobhan Lonergan who was capped four times for Ireland at senior level. Linked to this is the mother & son combination of Patricia Amond & Marcus Lawler and the father, mother and daughter combination of Brian McManus, Mary McManus (nee McKenna) and their daughter Catherine who won her first cap at the European Team Championships in June 2014. In addition to this the father & daughter combination of Mark & Katie Kirk who became the first father & daughter to win Irish senior titles since the championships began in 1873.

## With the removal of ‘the ban on foreign games’ 50 years ago, athletes from GAA backgrounds excelling in other sports has become common
09:00, 06 Mar 2021
Jack Regan made his second appearance in the Super Rugby Aotearoa series yesterday for The Highlanders as they beat The Chiefs in Hamilton, New Zealand.
‌
The Birr man has caught the eye having been named on 81-times capped All Black Justin Marshall’s Team of the Week, alongside Sam Whitelock in the second row, following his debut against reigning champions the Crusaders last weekend.
‌
The 23-year-old was deemed surplus to requirements by both Leinster and Ulster but has quickly rebuilt his career in New Zealand, playing at the highest level outside of international rugby in the sport’s most competitive environment.
Should he remain on his current trajectory, reintegration into the Irish system and international caps are likely to follow.
His father, Daithí, won an All-Ireland, four Leinster titles and a National League during his career with Offaly hurlers, as well as two All-Ireland club titles with Birr.
‌
With the removal of ‘the ban on foreign games’ 50 years ago, athletes from GAA backgrounds crossing over and excelling in other sports has become increasingly common.
Here are 10 of the standout examples.
‌
**Brendan and Shane Lowry**
Article continues below
The Lowrys have been at the coalface for some of the most iconic moments in Irish sport.
Article continues below
Brendan was a deadly corner-forward on the Offaly football team that sensationally put paid to Kerry’s five-in-a-row ambitions in the 1982 All-Ireland final, with his brothers Sean and Mick joining him on the team.
In 2009, his eldest son, Shane, was a promising amateur golfer who shocked the field at the Irish Open by taking the title, beating England’s Robert Rock in a dramatic play-off.
Article continues below
He immediately turned professional and won the Portugal Masters in 2012, the highly prestigious WGC Bridgestone in 2015 and was runner-up at the 2016 US Open after leading by four strokes entering the final round.

## With the removal of ‘the ban on foreign games’ 50 years ago, athletes from GAA backgrounds excelling in other sports has become common
He returned to winning ways in 2019 at the Abu Dhabi HSBC Championship in January followed by the crowning glory that July as he won a historic Open Championship on Irish soil in Portrush.
Article continues below
Lowry’s highest world ranking is 16, which he achieved in February of last year.
**Billy and Niall Quinn**
Article continues below
Article continues below
Billy Quinn was a terrific prospect for the Tipperary hurlers in the 1950s. He won successive All-Ireland minor titles in 1952 and ‘53 and graduated to the senior team the following year.
Quinn scored three goals from full-forward in Tipperary’s 3-10 to 1-4 victory over Kilkenny in that year’s National League final on no less a man than renowned full-back Jim ‘Diamond’ Hayden.
Article continues below
However, his promise largely went unfulfilled as he emigrated to London for three years and settled in Dublin on his return to Ireland, where he hurled for Faughs and briefly with Dublin. He died in 2016.
His son, Niall, hurled for Dublin minors in the 1983 All-Ireland final but was signed by Arsenal shortly afterwards. He scored on his debut against Liverpool in 1985 but struggled to win a regular first team place and a move to Manchester City in 1990 and saw an upturn in his fortunes.
Article continues below
Quinn scored a famous goal for Ireland against Holland at that year’s World Cup and eventually wound up as the country’s top scorer for a period with 21 goals from his 92 caps. He finished his career at Sunderland, where he later became chairman.
**Dan, Arthur, Donal and Dick Spring**
Article continues below
The Springs may be considered a political dynasty primarily but they also boast a rich sporting heritage.
Article continues below
Dan Spring was full-forward on Kerry’s All-Ireland winning teams of 1939 and ‘40, captaining the team to the latter success, before starting his 38-year run as a Labour TD for Kerry North in 1943.

## With the removal of ‘the ban on foreign games’ 50 years ago, athletes from GAA backgrounds excelling in other sports has become common
He died in 1988 but lived to see his son Dick serve as Labour Party leader, a position he held from 1982-97. Dick played both football and hurling for Kerry in the ‘70s but was better known as a rugby player, winning three caps for Ireland during the 1979 Five Nations while also being capped for Munster and representing London Irish.
Article continues below
Another sibling, Donal, played in seven rugby internationals between 1978-81, a time when caps were awarded far more sparingly than in the modern era. He also made 16 appearances for Munster, one of which was the famous win over New Zealand in 1978.
Dan Spring’s eldest son, Arthur, won an All-Ireland minor title with Kerry in 1963 but golf was his first love and he turned professional and joined the European Seniors Tour in 1995 following his 50th birthday. He also designed a number of courses before his passing in 2015.
Article continues below
**John and Mary Egan; John Egan Junior**
Article continues below
John Egan was an outstanding forward on the greatest Kerry team of all, winning six All-Irelands and five All Stars between 1975 and ‘84. He was captain of the Kerry team that came within minutes of a historic five-in-a-row in 1982.
Article continues below
A garda based in Cork, he died aged just 59 in 2012 and is immortalised in the shape of a statue in his native Sneem.
His son and namesake didn’t inherit all his sporting talents from his father, however, as his mother, Mary O’Halloran, also played for Kerry and won a League of Ireland medal with Cork Rangers.
Article continues below
The younger Egan was shifted around to a number of clubs in England before establishing himself with Gillingham, Brentford and currently Sheffield United, with whom he has played the last two seasons in the Premier League.

## With the removal of ‘the ban on foreign games’ 50 years ago, athletes from GAA backgrounds excelling in other sports has become common
Capped 12 times, the centre-back is now a regular for the Republic of Ireland and captained the international side for the first time against Bulgaria in September 2019.
Article continues below
**John and David Meyler**
Article continues below
John Meyler played inter-county hurling with his native Wexford and Cork, where he is a long-time resident, and won an All-Ireland hurling title as a non-playing sub with his adopted county in 1986, while he captained St Finbarr’s to an All-Ireland club football title the following year.
Article continues below
He is much-travelled as a manager having taken charge of Kerry twice, Wexford, Carlow and Cork, who he steered to a Munster title in 2018.
His son David was signed by Sunderland, then managed by Roy Keane, from Cork City in 2008 but enjoyed his best spell with Hull City and played in their 2014 FA Cup final defeat to Arsenal.
Article continues below
He won 26 caps for the Republic of Ireland, was part of Martin O’Neill’s squad at Euro 2016 and captained the side during the 2018 World Cup qualification campaign.
After difficult spells at Reading and Coventry City, he retired aged just 30 in 2019 due to persistent knee problems.
Article continues below
**Tim and Tadhg Kennelly**
Article continues below
Tim Kennelly was the defensive lynchpin on arguably the greatest Gaelic football team of all. ‘The Horse’ won five All-Irelands between 1975 and 1981, as well as being the All Star centre-back in 1979 and ‘80.
Article continues below
His son Noel won an All-Ireland with Kerry in 2000, by which time another son, Tadhg, was on the books of AFL club the Sydney Swans after an impressive underage career.

## Dooney Family Join Prestigious List
#### Dooney Family Become the 13th Father and Son to be Capped for Ireland at Senior Level
*Information compiled by Pierce O’Callaghan
Following on from Tuesday’s announcement that Conor Dooney (Raheny Shamrock AC) will now represent Ireland at the European Cross Country Championships in Bulgaria, the Dooney family have made a bit of history of their own. Conor’s father Roy Dooney was capped 19 times for Ireland at senior level. Together they become the 13th father and son to be capped for Ireland at senior level since 1876. Making it a real family affair younger brother Kevin will also be in the team representing Ireland in the U23 race in Bulgaria.

# Dooney Family Join Prestigious List - Athletics Ireland
## Dooney Family Join Prestigious List
#### Previous Father and Son Caps
The previous time this happened was earlier in the year with Eamon and John Coghlan when John gained his first cap at the Penn Relays in April. They join current father & son combinations of Tim & Timmy Crowe, Brendan & Shane Quinn, Paul & Colin Quirke.
Sara Treacy is the daughter of Siobhan Lonergan who was capped four times for Ireland at senior level. Linked to this is the mother & son combination of Patricia Amond & Marcus Lawler and the father, mother and daughter combination of Brian McManus, Mary McManus (nee McKenna) and their daughter Catherine who won her first cap at the European Team Championships in June 2014. In addition to this the father & daughter combination of Mark & Katie Kirk who became the first father & daughter to win Irish senior titles since the championships began in 1873.

## With the removal of ‘the ban on foreign games’ 50 years ago, athletes from GAA backgrounds excelling in other sports has become common
09:00, 06 Mar 2021
Jack Regan made his second appearance in the Super Rugby Aotearoa series yesterday for The Highlanders as they beat The Chiefs in Hamilton, New Zealand.
‌
The Birr man has caught the eye having been named on 81-times capped All Black Justin Marshall’s Team of the Week, alongside Sam Whitelock in the second row, following his debut against reigning champions the Crusaders last weekend.
‌
The 23-year-old was deemed surplus to requirements by both Leinster and Ulster but has quickly rebuilt his career in New Zealand, playing at the highest level outside of international rugby in the sport’s most competitive environment.
Should he remain on his current trajectory, reintegration into the Irish system and international caps are likely to follow.
His father, Daithí, won an All-Ireland, four Leinster titles and a National League during his career with Offaly hurlers, as well as two All-Ireland club titles with Birr.
‌
With the removal of ‘the ban on foreign games’ 50 years ago, athletes from GAA backgrounds crossing over and excelling in other sports has become increasingly common.
Here are 10 of the standout examples.
‌
**Brendan and Shane Lowry**
Article continues below
The Lowrys have been at the coalface for some of the most iconic moments in Irish sport.
Article continues below
Brendan was a deadly corner-forward on the Offaly football team that sensationally put paid to Kerry’s five-in-a-row ambitions in the 1982 All-Ireland final, with his brothers Sean and Mick joining him on the team.
In 2009, his eldest son, Shane, was a promising amateur golfer who shocked the field at the Irish Open by taking the title, beating England’s Robert Rock in a dramatic play-off.
Article continues below
He immediately turned professional and won the Portugal Masters in 2012, the highly prestigious WGC Bridgestone in 2015 and was runner-up at the 2016 US Open after leading by four strokes entering the final round.
texts.1:
## With the removal of ‘the ban on foreign games’ 50 years ago, athletes from GAA backgrounds excelling in other sports has become common
He returned to winning ways in 2019 at the Abu Dhabi HSBC Championship in January followed by the crowning glory that July as he won a historic Open Championship on Irish soil in Portrush.
Article continues below
Lowry’s highest world ranking is 16, which he achieved in February of last year.
**Billy and Niall Quinn**
Article continues below
Article continues below
Billy Quinn was a terrific prospect for the Tipperary hurlers in the 1950s. He won successive All-Ireland minor titles in 1952 and ‘53 and graduated to the senior team the following year.
Quinn scored three goals from full-forward in Tipperary’s 3-10 to 1-4 victory over Kilkenny in that year’s National League final on no less a man than renowned full-back Jim ‘Diamond’ Hayden.
Article continues below
However, his promise largely went unfulfilled as he emigrated to London for three years and settled in Dublin on his return to Ireland, where he hurled for Faughs and briefly with Dublin. He died in 2016.
His son, Niall, hurled for Dublin minors in the 1983 All-Ireland final but was signed by Arsenal shortly afterwards. He scored on his debut against Liverpool in 1985 but struggled to win a regular first team place and a move to Manchester City in 1990 and saw an upturn in his fortunes.
Article continues below
Quinn scored a famous goal for Ireland against Holland at that year’s World Cup and eventually wound up as the country’s top scorer for a period with 21 goals from his 92 caps. He finished his career at Sunderland, where he later became chairman.
**Dan, Arthur, Donal and Dick Spring**
Article continues below
The Springs may be considered a political dynasty primarily but they also boast a rich sporting heritage.
Article continues below
Dan Spring was full-forward on Kerry’s All-Ireland winning teams of 1939 and ‘40, captaining the team to the latter success, before starting his 38-year run as a Labour TD for Kerry North in 1943.
texts.2:
## With the removal of ‘the ban on foreign games’ 50 years ago, athletes from GAA backgrounds excelling in other sports has become common
He died in 1988 but lived to see his son Dick serve as Labour Party leader, a position he held from 1982-97. Dick played both football and hurling for Kerry in the ‘70s but was better known as a rugby player, winning three caps for Ireland during the 1979 Five Nations while also being capped for Munster and representing London Irish.
Article continues below
Another sibling, Donal, played in seven rugby internationals between 1978-81, a time when caps were awarded far more sparingly than in the modern era. He also made 16 appearances for Munster, one of which was the famous win over New Zealand in 1978.
Dan Spring’s eldest son, Arthur, won an All-Ireland minor title with Kerry in 1963 but golf was his first love and he turned professional and joined the European Seniors Tour in 1995 following his 50th birthday. He also designed a number of courses before his passing in 2015.
Article continues below
**John and Mary Egan; John Egan Junior**
Article continues below
John Egan was an outstanding forward on the greatest Kerry team of all, winning six All-Irelands and five All Stars between 1975 and ‘84. He was captain of the Kerry team that came within minutes of a historic five-in-a-row in 1982.
Article continues below
A garda based in Cork, he died aged just 59 in 2012 and is immortalised in the shape of a statue in his native Sneem.
His son and namesake didn’t inherit all his sporting talents from his father, however, as his mother, Mary O’Halloran, also played for Kerry and won a League of Ireland medal with Cork Rangers.
Article continues below
The younger Egan was shifted around to a number of clubs in England before establishing himself with Gillingham, Brentford and currently Sheffield United, with whom he has played the last two seasons in the Premier League.
texts.3:
## With the removal of ‘the ban on foreign games’ 50 years ago, athletes from GAA backgrounds excelling in other sports has become common
Capped 12 times, the centre-back is now a regular for the Republic of Ireland and captained the international side for the first time against Bulgaria in September 2019.
Article continues below
**John and David Meyler**
Article continues below
John Meyler played inter-county hurling with his native Wexford and Cork, where he is a long-time resident, and won an All-Ireland hurling title as a non-playing sub with his adopted county in 1986, while he captained St Finbarr’s to an All-Ireland club football title the following year.
Article continues below
He is much-travelled as a manager having taken charge of Kerry twice, Wexford, Carlow and Cork, who he steered to a Munster title in 2018.
His son David was signed by Sunderland, then managed by Roy Keane, from Cork City in 2008 but enjoyed his best spell with Hull City and played in their 2014 FA Cup final defeat to Arsenal.
Article continues below
He won 26 caps for the Republic of Ireland, was part of Martin O’Neill’s squad at Euro 2016 and captained the side during the 2018 World Cup qualification campaign.
After difficult spells at Reading and Coventry City, he retired aged just 30 in 2019 due to persistent knee problems.
Article continues below
**Tim and Tadhg Kennelly**
Article continues below
Tim Kennelly was the defensive lynchpin on arguably the greatest Gaelic football team of all. ‘The Horse’ won five All-Irelands between 1975 and 1981, as well as being the All Star centre-back in 1979 and ‘80.
Article continues below
His son Noel won an All-Ireland with Kerry in 2000, by which time another son, Tadhg, was on the books of AFL club the Sydney Swans after an impressive underage career.

## With the removal of ‘the ban on foreign games’ 50 years ago, athletes from GAA backgrounds excelling in other sports has become common
09:00, 06 Mar 2021
Jack Regan made his second appearance in the Super Rugby Aotearoa series yesterday for The Highlanders as they beat The Chiefs in Hamilton, New Zealand.
‌
The Birr man has caught the eye having been named on 81-times capped All Black Justin Marshall’s Team of the Week, alongside Sam Whitelock in the second row, following his debut against reigning champions the Crusaders last weekend.
‌
The 23-year-old was deemed surplus to requirements by both Leinster and Ulster but has quickly rebuilt his career in New Zealand, playing at the highest level outside of international rugby in the sport’s most competitive environment.
Should he remain on his current trajectory, reintegration into the Irish system and international caps are likely to follow.
His father, Daithí, won an All-Ireland, four Leinster titles and a National League during his career with Offaly hurlers, as well as two All-Ireland club titles with Birr.
‌
With the removal of ‘the ban on foreign games’ 50 years ago, athletes from GAA backgrounds crossing over and excelling in other sports has become increasingly common.
Here are 10 of the standout examples.
‌
**Brendan and Shane Lowry**
Article continues below
The Lowrys have been at the coalface for some of the most iconic moments in Irish sport.
Article continues below
Brendan was a deadly corner-forward on the Offaly football team that sensationally put paid to Kerry’s five-in-a-row ambitions in the 1982 All-Ireland final, with his brothers Sean and Mick joining him on the team.
In 2009, his eldest son, Shane, was a promising amateur golfer who shocked the field at the Irish Open by taking the title, beating England’s Robert Rock in a dramatic play-off.
Article continues below
He immediately turned professional and won the Portugal Masters in 2012, the highly prestigious WGC Bridgestone in 2015 and was runner-up at the 2016 US Open after leading by four strokes entering the final round.

## With the removal of ‘the ban on foreign games’ 50 years ago, athletes from GAA backgrounds excelling in other sports has become common
He returned to winning ways in 2019 at the Abu Dhabi HSBC Championship in January followed by the crowning glory that July as he won a historic Open Championship on Irish soil in Portrush.
Article continues below
Lowry’s highest world ranking is 16, which he achieved in February of last year.
**Billy and Niall Quinn**
Article continues below
Article continues below
Billy Quinn was a terrific prospect for the Tipperary hurlers in the 1950s. He won successive All-Ireland minor titles in 1952 and ‘53 and graduated to the senior team the following year.
Quinn scored three goals from full-forward in Tipperary’s 3-10 to 1-4 victory over Kilkenny in that year’s National League final on no less a man than renowned full-back Jim ‘Diamond’ Hayden.
Article continues below
However, his promise largely went unfulfilled as he emigrated to London for three years and settled in Dublin on his return to Ireland, where he hurled for Faughs and briefly with Dublin. He died in 2016.
His son, Niall, hurled for Dublin minors in the 1983 All-Ireland final but was signed by Arsenal shortly afterwards. He scored on his debut against Liverpool in 1985 but struggled to win a regular first team place and a move to Manchester City in 1990 and saw an upturn in his fortunes.
Article continues below
Quinn scored a famous goal for Ireland against Holland at that year’s World Cup and eventually wound up as the country’s top scorer for a period with 21 goals from his 92 caps. He finished his career at Sunderland, where he later became chairman.
**Dan, Arthur, Donal and Dick Spring**
Article continues below
The Springs may be considered a political dynasty primarily but they also boast a rich sporting heritage.
Article continues below
Dan Spring was full-forward on Kerry’s All-Ireland winning teams of 1939 and ‘40, captaining the team to the latter success, before starting his 38-year run as a Labour TD for Kerry North in 1943.

## With the removal of ‘the ban on foreign games’ 50 years ago, athletes from GAA backgrounds excelling in other sports has become common
He died in 1988 but lived to see his son Dick serve as Labour Party leader, a position he held from 1982-97. Dick played both football and hurling for Kerry in the ‘70s but was better known as a rugby player, winning three caps for Ireland during the 1979 Five Nations while also being capped for Munster and representing London Irish.
Article continues below
Another sibling, Donal, played in seven rugby internationals between 1978-81, a time when caps were awarded far more sparingly than in the modern era. He also made 16 appearances for Munster, one of which was the famous win over New Zealand in 1978.
Dan Spring’s eldest son, Arthur, won an All-Ireland minor title with Kerry in 1963 but golf was his first love and he turned professional and joined the European Seniors Tour in 1995 following his 50th birthday. He also designed a number of courses before his passing in 2015.
Article continues below
**John and Mary Egan; John Egan Junior**
Article continues below
John Egan was an outstanding forward on the greatest Kerry team of all, winning six All-Irelands and five All Stars between 1975 and ‘84. He was captain of the Kerry team that came within minutes of a historic five-in-a-row in 1982.
Article continues below
A garda based in Cork, he died aged just 59 in 2012 and is immortalised in the shape of a statue in his native Sneem.
His son and namesake didn’t inherit all his sporting talents from his father, however, as his mother, Mary O’Halloran, also played for Kerry and won a League of Ireland medal with Cork Rangers.
Article continues below
The younger Egan was shifted around to a number of clubs in England before establishing himself with Gillingham, Brentford and currently Sheffield United, with whom he has played the last two seasons in the Premier League.

## With the removal of ‘the ban on foreign games’ 50 years ago, athletes from GAA backgrounds excelling in other sports has become common
Capped 12 times, the centre-back is now a regular for the Republic of Ireland and captained the international side for the first time against Bulgaria in September 2019.
Article continues below
**John and David Meyler**
Article continues below
John Meyler played inter-county hurling with his native Wexford and Cork, where he is a long-time resident, and won an All-Ireland hurling title as a non-playing sub with his adopted county in 1986, while he captained St Finbarr’s to an All-Ireland club football title the following year.
Article continues below
He is much-travelled as a manager having taken charge of Kerry twice, Wexford, Carlow and Cork, who he steered to a Munster title in 2018.
His son David was signed by Sunderland, then managed by Roy Keane, from Cork City in 2008 but enjoyed his best spell with Hull City and played in their 2014 FA Cup final defeat to Arsenal.
Article continues below
He won 26 caps for the Republic of Ireland, was part of Martin O’Neill’s squad at Euro 2016 and captained the side during the 2018 World Cup qualification campaign.
After difficult spells at Reading and Coventry City, he retired aged just 30 in 2019 due to persistent knee problems.
Article continues below
**Tim and Tadhg Kennelly**
Article continues below
Tim Kennelly was the defensive lynchpin on arguably the greatest Gaelic football team of all. ‘The Horse’ won five All-Irelands between 1975 and 1981, as well as being the All Star centre-back in 1979 and ‘80.
Article continues below
His son Noel won an All-Ireland with Kerry in 2000, by which time another son, Tadhg, was on the books of AFL club the Sydney Swans after an impressive underage career.

# Donore Harriers - The committee were sad to hear of the... | Facebook
## Donore Harriers's Post
[December 17, 2021](https://www.facebook.com/donoreharriersac/posts/pfbid033dEmj6pSkc8BeWzxo3DTGBEtaXz6EYhNUPqVk18Uk5BQNCbogPaSSTN75KE7dFHcl?__cft__[0]=AZjMRDBrM3ht344hHX51S6tCdIhDab74ucuRObLv9AiBs0QIsSefJb1c8kY-rhr-x9J5ex0Olzxj0k2tkWFH5MzqZRwKC5fb0Q2PhOj2ztfVzgXwx8Ycgpdq_weVb4m5fc7tQDida6Ya667m_vc05CRwf_mfCMrT&__tn__=%2CO%2CP-R) ·
The committee were sad to hear of the death of former member, Tommy Hopkins, at the age of 74, at his home in the US, after being ill for the last year or so.
Tommy and his brothers Jim and Des were stalwarts of Donore Harriers in the 1960's and 1970's. Their father, Tom, was also a club member, and their sister Emily (Dowling) is well known in running circles with Sportsworld AC.
Tommy represented Ireland in international cross country events in 1966 and 1967 at the age of 18 and 19, and went on scholarship to the US in 1967.
The committee and members of Donore Harriers extend our condolences to Tommie's family.
(Photo of the 1962 Donore harriers opening run - Tommy Hopkins back row last on the right )

# Donore Harriers - The committee were sad to hear of the... | Facebook
## Donore Harriers's Post
[December 17, 2021](https://www.facebook.com/donoreharriersac/posts/pfbid033dEmj6pSkc8BeWzxo3DTGBEtaXz6EYhNUPqVk18Uk5BQNCbogPaSSTN75KE7dFHcl?__cft__[0]=AZjMRDBrM3ht344hHX51S6tCdIhDab74ucuRObLv9AiBs0QIsSefJb1c8kY-rhr-x9J5ex0Olzxj0k2tkWFH5MzqZRwKC5fb0Q2PhOj2ztfVzgXwx8Ycgpdq_weVb4m5fc7tQDida6Ya667m_vc05CRwf_mfCMrT&__tn__=%2CO%2CP-R) ·
The committee were sad to hear of the death of former member, Tommy Hopkins, at the age of 74, at his home in the US, after being ill for the last year or so.
Tommy and his brothers Jim and Des were stalwarts of Donore Harriers in the 1960's and 1970's. Their father, Tom, was also a club member, and their sister Emily (Dowling) is well known in running circles with Sportsworld AC.
Tommy represented Ireland in international cross country events in 1966 and 1967 at the age of 18 and 19, and went on scholarship to the US in 1967.
The committee and members of Donore Harriers extend our condolences to Tommie's family.
(Photo of the 1962 Donore harriers opening run - Tommy Hopkins back row last on the right )

# Donore Harriers - The committee were sad to hear of the... | Facebook
## Donore Harriers's Post
[December 17, 2021](https://www.facebook.com/donoreharriersac/posts/pfbid033dEmj6pSkc8BeWzxo3DTGBEtaXz6EYhNUPqVk18Uk5BQNCbogPaSSTN75KE7dFHcl?__cft__[0]=AZjMRDBrM3ht344hHX51S6tCdIhDab74ucuRObLv9AiBs0QIsSefJb1c8kY-rhr-x9J5ex0Olzxj0k2tkWFH5MzqZRwKC5fb0Q2PhOj2ztfVzgXwx8Ycgpdq_weVb4m5fc7tQDida6Ya667m_vc05CRwf_mfCMrT&__tn__=%2CO%2CP-R) ·
The committee were sad to hear of the death of former member, Tommy Hopkins, at the age of 74, at his home in the US, after being ill for the last year or so.
Tommy and his brothers Jim and Des were stalwarts of Donore Harriers in the 1960's and 1970's. Their father, Tom, was also a club member, and their sister Emily (Dowling) is well known in running circles with Sportsworld AC.
Tommy represented Ireland in international cross country events in 1966 and 1967 at the age of 18 and 19, and went on scholarship to the US in 1967.
The committee and members of Donore Harriers extend our condolences to Tommie's family.
(Photo of the 1962 Donore harriers opening run - Tommy Hopkins back row last on the right )

steps.text:
Based on my research, the unique Irish athletics family where **father, son, and daughter** were all capped for Ireland is the **Hopkins family**. Here are the details:

## **The Hopkins Family**

| Family Member | Role | First Cap Year | Event/Competition |
|--------------|------|---------------|-------------------|
| **Tom Hopkins** | Father | **1938** | International Cross Country, Belfast (2 April 1938) |
| **Tommy Hopkins** | Son | **1967** | International Cross Country, Barry (18 March 1967) |
| **Emily Hopkins** (née Hopkins, married name Dowling) | Daughter | **1967** | International Cross Country, Barry (18 March 1967) |

### Key Facts:
- **Tom Hopkins** (born 19 July 1910) made his international debut in 1938 when he was 28 years old
- **Tommy Hopkins** (born 14 July 1947) followed 29 years later, making his debut at age 19 in 1967
- **Emily Hopkins** (later Dowling) also made her debut in **1967**, just weeks after her brother Tommy, at age approximately 15-16
- All three competed in cross country events, primarily through Sportsworld AC in Dublin

This family holds the distinction of being the only Irish athletics family with three generations (father, son, and daughter) all representing Ireland at senior international level. They are officially recorded in Athletics Ireland's statistics as one of the few families with "Multiple Ireland caps from one family."

*Note: There is a separate famous British athlete named Thelma Hopkins (Olympic silver medalist 1956) but she competed for Northern Ireland/Great Britain, not the Irish athletics team.*
